articles.title: She left home for gymnastics. She is now the only Indian gymnast selected for Asian Games: This is Pranati Nayak
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: There are moments in an athlete's career when winning a medal is no longer the only measure of success. For Pranati Nayak, simply continuin.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: There are moments in an athlete's career when winning a medal is no longer the only measure of success. For Pranati Nayak, simply continuing to stand on the gymnastics floor has become part of the journey.The 31-year-old from West Bengal is preparing for her fourth Asian Games, a remarkable milestone in a career that has taken her from leaving her family behind as a young girl to representing India at the Olympics. She is also the lone Indian gymnast selected for the 2026 Asian Games, where she will compete in the women's vault and all-around events.Her journey began with a difficult choice. Pursuing gymnastics meant moving away from home and family at a young age of eight. What followed was years of training, travelling, injuries and the constant pressure that comes with trying to stay relevant in a sport where careers can be brutally short.Yet Nayak kept returning.She became the second Indian woman gymnast to qualify for the Olympics when she competed at Tokyo 2020. She has also built a reputation as one of India's most consistent vaulters, winning Asian Championships bronze in 2019 and 2022. The 2022 medal made her the first Indian gymnast to win two medals at the Asian Championships.But the road has not been smooth.In 2026, injury forced her to miss the national championships. Instead of allowing another setback to define her season, Nayak returned strongly at the FIG World Challenge Cup in Tashkent in May, winning silver in vault with a score of 13.025.That comeback is important because Nayak's career has increasingly become about finding a way forward after difficult moments.Her recent Commonwealth Games experience in Glasgow also left her disappointed, but rather than allowing the setback to linger, she has turned her attention towards Nagoya. The Asian Games offer another chance to get her routines right on a major international stage.More than a gymnastAway from competition, Nayak has spoken about the importance of meditation, discipline and managing pressure. She also mentors younger gymnasts, passing on lessons from a career that has already included an Olympics, Asian Games appearances and multiple international medals.That may be the most unusual part of her story.When Nayak first left home to pursue gymnastics, the destination could hardly have been guaranteed. There was no promise of an Olympic appearance or a long international career. There was only the decision to keep training.More than a decade later, she is still making that choice.Nagoya will bring another challenge. The vault remains her speciality, but she will also compete in the all-around event. A medal would add another chapter to an already long career.But for Nayak, the Asian Games are also about something more personal, proving that the sacrifices made by a young girl who left home to chase gymnastics were worth it.At her fourth Asian Games, she is no longer the teenager who had to leave everything familiar behind.She is the veteran who has survived the injuries, the disappointments and the changing generations of Indian gymnastics and has kept coming back.For Pranati Nayak, perhaps that is the victory that matters most.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: NYC triathlete Lin Chung dies at 34, found unconscious in swimming pool during Hamptons race
articles.summary: International Sports News: Lin Chung, a 34-year-old Queens resident, died after he was found unconscious during the swimming portion of the Mighty Hamptons Steve Tarpinian Memor.
articles.body: Lin Chung, a 34-year-old Queens resident, died after he was found unconscious during the swimming portion of the Mighty Hamptons Steve Tarpinian Memorial Triathlon in Sag Harbor on Sunday.Chung was competing in the 1.5 km swim when lifeguards noticed he was in distress in Noyack Bay. He was pulled from the water and given emergency medical treatment before being taken to a nearby hospital.Lin Chung dies during 1.5 km swim in Noyack BayLin Chung was taking part in the swim leg of the Mighty Hamptons Steve Tarpinian Memorial Triathlon on September 13, 2026. The event includes swimming, cycling and running, with the opening swim taking place in the waters off Long Beach in Sag Harbor.According to police and event officials, lifeguards saw Chung in trouble and quickly moved to rescue him. Other competitors also helped bring him out of the water.A group of swimmers used a paddleboard to get Chung to safety. A lifeguard immediately began performing CPR while the group worked to keep him on the board.Fellow triathlete Bill Hughes described the rescue effort to the Southampton Press.“We got him up on the paddleboard and then we- it was me and several women, I think the wave right before me must have been mostly women, we were kicking as hard as we could to try go keep him on the paddleboard,” Hughes said.“The lifeguard was doing CPR, chest compressions and turning him on his side and we were all working really hard to keep him from falling off the wet board. All credit to that lifeguard, I don’t know who the man was but it was a heroic effort by him”, he added.Additional lifeguards and police officers joined the emergency response after Chung was brought out of the water. An automated external defibrillator was also used as efforts to save him continued.Despite the emergency response, Chung could not be revived. He was transported to Stony Brook Southampton Hospital, where he was later pronounced dead.EventPower released a statement following the incident.“We are deeply saddened to confirm the death of a male athlete who suffered a medical emergency during the swim portion of yesterday’s Mighty Hamptons Triathlon,” the organizer said.“Our sport of triathlon lost a member of our beloved community. We extend our deepest condolences to the athlete’s family and friends and we offer them our support as they go through this unimaginable time”, the statement added.Officials have not announced what caused Chung’s death. The Suffolk County Medical Examiner’s Office is handling the investigation.The incident comes less than two weeks after another triathlete, Spencer Korwin, died in nearby Shelter Island. Korwin, a 38-year-old Manhattan resident and former Team USA triathlete, disappeared after going for a morning swim during a family vacation on September 2.A large search operation was launched after Korwin went missing near the Pridwin Hotel. His body was later found underneath the dock from where he had entered the water.In Chung’s case, officials have not said whether water conditions played a role. The investigation into his death remains ongoing.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Penta's Time as WWE Champion is Coming
articles.summary: One thing was apparent in the closing moments of Monday's WWE Raw, when Penta looked back at the ring and appeared to acknowledge World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns following their blockbuster main event: the masked luchador's time as world champion in pro wrestling's most prominent company is coming, perhaps sooner rather than later.
articles.body:
One thing was apparent in the closing moments of Monday's WWE Raw, when Penta looked back at the ring and appeared to acknowledge World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns following their blockbuster main event: the masked luchador's time as world champion in pro wrestling's most prominent company is coming, perhaps sooner rather than later.

Penta challenged Reigns in the marquee match-up of WWE's TV return to Mexico City, and while he failed to dethrone The OTC in front of his fellow countrymen, he proved to the wrestling world that he is a legitimate main event star.

In what may have been the biggest, most important match of his career, the veteran competitor rose to the occasion, picking this contest, against the biggest star in the company, to have what was arguably his best match in a WWE ring.

If that match and that spot were a test, he passed it with flying colors.

Neither fazed by the reaction of the crowd nor the magnitude of the moment, he went toe-to-toe with the industry's measuring stick and never looked overwhelmed or out of place. He stood confidently, face-to-face with Reigns from the opening bell and was his equal through every second of the match.

His excellence in the match is not some revelation, either.

From his debut in WWE before WrestleMania 41, the masked Superstar has made a habit of passing tests and rising to the occasion. Some worried that the language barrier would prevent him from maximizing his star power. Instead, he showcased his natural charisma on the mic and through his body language, and the fans ate it up.

Between the ropes, there has never been a doubt about his abilities, be it in AEW, TNA, or dating back as far as Lucha Underground. In all three promotions, televised for the world to see, he was among (if not the ) best wrestlers in the world.

Still, despite his proven track record, WWE is a different beast entirely. Some of the finest professional wrestlers have crumbled under the bright lights and crippling expectations that come with setting foot on that stage.

He has risen to the occasion every time, including this past April at WrestleMania 42, when he nearly stole the show in the Ladder Match for the Intercontinental Championship, alongside Rey Mysterio, Je'Von Evans, Dragon Lee, Rusev, and JD McDonagh.

A performer whose connection with the audience, regardless of the location, is unwavering, he checks every box needed to be a legitimate main event star and world champion in WWE.

Now, he has a signature performance against one of the cornerstones of the promotion to his name.

At a time when WWE has changed things up and finally allowed someone like Sami Zayn to run with the top prize in the company, paying off years of hard work and dedication, Penta has an even higher potential upside, thanks to the amount of merchandise he can move and the connection he has with the kids in the audience.

He has endeared himself to the adults who think he is cool, the kids who are dazzled by his athletic ability between the ropes and larger-than-life persona, and the die-hards who already know how great he is.

It is time to pay off his steady rise up the ranks by putting the title on him and seeing what he can do. Like Rey Mysterio before him, Penta has the tools necessary to transcend lucha libre and become one of the most decorated, celebrated, and beloved masked Superstars in pro wrestling history, with at least one world title on his resume.

After Monday's defining performance, it is only a matter of time before he joins one of his idols in the stratosphere.

articles.title: Anthony Martial turns down lucrative move despite being without a club
articles.summary: 3Anthony Martial ended his Manchester United career in the summer of 2024 after a nine-year stay at Old Trafford that ultimately failed to live up to the hyp...
articles.body:
Anthony Martial ended his Manchester United career in the summer of 2024 after a nine-year stay at Old Trafford that ultimately failed to live up to the hype which surrounded his transfer from Monaco as a potential teenage sensation.

The French forward got off to the perfect start with a sublime goal against Liverpool on his debut under the tutelage of Louis van Gaal, who spent a record-breaking fee for a teenager to bring him to Manchester.

However, the best part of £50 million never translated to consistent performances on the pitch, with his debut wonder strike arguably remaining the highlight of his stay at the club.

Since leaving United, Martial has struggled to find his feet at either AEK Athens or Mexican side Monterrey after his loan spell with Sevilla failed to do enough to impress the Spanish outfit to take him on permanently when he officially cut ties with United.

He is now without a club and assessing his options after leaving Mexico under a cloud after a wretched season in North America.

As reported by footmercato.net , Martial has been offered a huge fee to make a shock move to North Africa, with Libyan outfit Al-Ittihad SC contacting him about a potential deal.

The report suggests the Libyans were ready to shell out a whopping €10 million over two seasons, with a €5 million signing-on bonus to secure his services after already signing former Premier League star Sofiane Boufal this summer.

However, Martial is said to have no interest in a move to Africa, as he "favours a real sporting project over the economic aspect for the rest of his career," according to the outlet.

The 30-year-old looks keen to return to Europe after his Mexican nightmare, with Malaga the favourites for his signature as he attempts to revive his career for one final push in the big leagues.

United, meanwhile, are still struggling to find the formula to consistently perform at the top level, much as they did during Martial's time at the club, with seemingly not much changing since his departure.

Michael Carrick is currently experimenting with an attacking line-up that shifts from a false nine to an out-and-out striker, given the lack of depth and quality in the squad.

The struggles up top were underlined in the powderpuff derby defeat to neighbours Manchester City , who managed to keep United at bay with relative ease despite having ten men for the majority of Sunday's game.

United will hope to find their shooting boots tonight as Brighton travel to Old Trafford looking to continue their excellent record at the Theatre of Dreams and knock Carrick's men out of the Carabao Cup in the third round.

Defeat would leave Carrick under huge pressure given the lacklustre start to the season and therefore INEOS, who will also be feeling the heat after an underwhelming transfer window looks to have left the manager facing the campaign with one hand tied behind his back.

articles.title: F1 2027 Calendar: Full Race Schedule And Sprint Venues
articles.summary: Formula 1 has revealed the calendar for the 2027 season, featuring 24 races, a record 10 sprint events and the return of Portugal and Turkey.
articles.body:
Formula 1 has announced the calendar for the 2027 season, featuring 24 races and a record 10 sprint events .

Bahrain will kick off the season on March 12-14, returning as the opener after Australia took over the slot in 2025 and 2026. The championship will then head to neighboring Saudi Arabia for the second leg of the season's first double header.

Australia now slots in as the third round, setting off a triple header with Japan and China.

Next, F1 will make its first of three visits to the United States with the Miami Grand Prix from April 30 to May 2 before heading to Montreal, Canada, after a two-week break.

The European leg of the season will then kick off with Monaco on June 4-6, followed by Portugal, which makes a return to the calendar on a two-year deal, having hosted races in 2020 and 2021 during the pandemic.

The legendary Silverstone circuit will form a double header with Austria's Red Bull Ring before Spa-Francorchamps launches another double header with Hungaroring in Hungary.

Following a rotational deal with Barcelona, the Belgian Grand Prix at Spa will now be held in odd-numbered years from 2027, while the Spanish race will feature in even-numbered years starting from 2028.

After a month-long break, F1 will head to Italy's Monza for a double header with the brand-new Madring circuit, which debuted in 2026 and hosted Madrid's first race in over 40 years.

Like Portugal, Istanbul is returning to the calendar for the first time since 2021, with the Turkish Grand Prix taking place on October 1-3 between Azerbaijan and Singapore, forming a triple header.

The Circuit of the Americas in Austin will launch another triple header with Mexico and Brazil in late October, before the series heads back to the U.S. for the third and final stop on American soil at the Las Vegas Grand Prix in November.

F1 will then make one more trip to the Middle East for the penultimate round in Lusail, Qatar, before the season concludes at Yas Marina in Abu Dhabi on December 10-12.

As for the sprint, the number of the events will increase from six to a record 10, with Bahrain, Australia, Japan, Monaco and Abu Dhabi all set to host the short race for the first time.

Montreal, Silverstone, Monza, Sao Paulo and Lusail will also return as sprint venues for 2027.

"The 2027 calendar brings together some of the most iconic circuits and vibrant cities in the world, creating an incredible stage for another unforgettable season of Formula 1," said Stefano Domenicali, president and CEO of F1.

"We are thrilled to welcome Portugal and Türkiye to the championship and to expand Sprint racing to ten events, giving our fans even more intensity, drama, and the wheel-to-wheel action that make our sport so special."

Here's the full schedule for the 24-race season, with sprint events marked (*).

12. Belgian Grand Prix, Spa-Francorchamps

The 2027 pre-season testing will take place in Sakhir, Bahrain, on February 24–27.

articles.title: Oregon's main problem before USC: Ducks have more than one problem
articles.summary: Oregon's problems can't be reduced to one coach or player. It's a sign of hope for USC with September 26 coming closer
articles.body:
USC plays Oregon in just over a week. One big problem for the Ducks right now: They have more than one problem. They were bad on both sides of the ball against Oklahoma State . This goes beyond one coach or player, as Ducks Wire noted:

"Flipping now to the coordinators, neither was even close to good enough on Saturday. Offensively, the Ducks were out of rhythm and out of sync for the second game in a row, amassing just 281 yards of offense and 12 first downs in the game, punting five times. Defensively, things were just as bad: a unit billed as arguably the best in the nation gave up 554 total yards, including 317 through the air and 237 on the ground. Cowboys quarterback Drew Mestemaker threw for 317 yards and rushed for 109 yards on his own. The Ducks allowed Oklahoma State 12 explosive plays in the game.

"While the players are the ones on the field and will get a ton of direct criticism, anyone casting shade needs to start with the guys on the sideline. Going into a year where there were such high expectations, Lanning took a risk and hired a pair of inside guys who were on the team, rather than going national and getting big names. On Saturday, that looked like a tough decision. Time will tell if it pans out. This loss is absolutely on Dan Lanning and his staff for not having their team prepared, and it will be a mark on his resume until he can finally win the big game."

Oregon and Dan Lanning having to replace two coordinators has not worked out well for the Ducks. Lanning doesn't have to worry about one side of the ball; he has to worry about both, and get them both in order before facing USC. The Trojans hope the Ducks don't have enough time to fix everything they have to fix.

USC wraps up nonconference play with victory over Louisiana

articles.title: Cameron Boozer Has Chance to Become Best Player in Grizzlies History
articles.summary: Cameron Boozer has not played an NBA game yet, but he has a chance to eventually surpass Marc Gasol, Pau Gasol and Ja Morant in Grizzlies history.
articles.body:
The Memphis Grizzlies have rostered a lot of talented players in their history, but few true superstars. Rookie Cameron Boozer has a chance to be the best player to ever put on their jersey .

That might sound bold. A review of Grizzlies history vindicates the claim. It's not a particularly high bar to clear, but that doesn't mean it will be easy, either.

Shareef Abdur-Rahim Was the Original Grizzlies Star

Younger readers may not know that the Grizzlies once resided in Canada. For their first six seasons, they were the Vancouver Grizzlies.

Abdur-Rahim was an impressive, well-rounded forward. His best season came in 1998-99, when he averaged 23.0 points, 7.5 rebounds, 3.4 assists, 1.4 steals, and 1.1 blocks per game.

For Abdur-Rahim, the numbers didn't seem to match the impact. It's possible that he was a victim of poor roster construction, but he never seemed to impact winning very much. His career-high 2.2 Box Plus/Minus (BPM) is more indicative of a role player than a star.

Realistically, he isn't the best player in the franchise's history.

Pau and Marc Gasol Set the Standard in Memphis

When the Grizzlies moved from Vancouver to Memphis, they replaced Abdur-Rahim with a similarly well-rounded big man. In 2005-06, Pau Gasol averaged 20.4 points, 8.9 rebounds, and 4.6 assists per game. His ability to make plays for his teammates was exceptional for a 7-footer.

His career-high 5.5 BPM came in Memphis. He was a bona fide star. Unlike Abdur-Rahim, he was able to get the Grizzlies to the postseason, but after three straight first-round exits, he was sent to the Los Angeles Lakers .

Ironically, in that deal, they acquired the draft rights to Pau's younger brother. Marc Gasol was the 2012-13 NBA Defensive Player of the Year, and he was always in the running for the award. He was also a playmaking hub. Gasol was the face of the Grit-and-Grind Grizzlies, and a lot of fans would call him the best player in franchise history.

Ja Morant Became the Grizzlies' Biggest Star

It's painful, recent history, but this article would be remiss not to mention Ja Morant.

On a surface level, he's put up the best stats in franchise history. Morant averaged 27.4 points per game in 2021-22. It was the highest points-per-game average in franchise history by a comfortable margin.

Unfortunately, if you're reading this, you know what went wrong. Morant was regularly injured and suspended, to the point that the team finally moved him . If you're offensively minded enough, you may rank him over Gasol.

But you're surely hoping Boozer can surpass him in franchise history.

Cameron Boozer Has a Chance to Pass Them All

Longevity is the factor that should put Boozer ahead of Morant. Playoff success and offensive production could put him over Gasol.

We're getting ahead of ourselves. Boozer hasn't played a regular-season game yet . There are many possible outcomes for his career.

But one of them is him being the best player in Grizzlies history.

articles.title: ACC Preview # 18 – Duke, Part I
articles.summary: Last season ended poorly, but this season, Duke is loaded for bear.
articles.body:
A lot of people thought Duke would fall off when Mike Krzyzewski retired. It didn't happen.

When Coach K announced in June 2021 that he would step away after the 2021-22 season, some mocked him and accused him of wanting a farewell tour. More thoughtful observers figured he had a plan. He did.

Duke named Jon Scheyer his successor, which let Krzyzewski work even more closely with his young protege and gave Scheyer time to recruit his own players. The result has been one of the most successful handoffs from a legendary coach to his successor in the history of the sport.

Scheyer has done a brilliant job so far, and has adapted to the new era as well as any coach in the country. His ACC record is 65-13 (.833); his overall mark is 124-25 (.832). After a Sweet Sixteen in his first season, he took Duke to the Elite Eight in 2023-24, the Final Four in 2024-25, and the Elite Eight again last season.

Scheyer and Duke took plenty of grief for how that Elite Eight game against UConn ended. As you'll no doubt remember, the Blue Devils built a 19-point lead, UConn rallied, and Cayden Boozer turned the ball over in the final seconds. Braylon Mullins hit a shot for the ages, and that is what everyone remembers.

What people tend to forget is that Caleb Foster and Patrick Ngongba spent most of the tournament on scooters. Ngongba played against UConn, but he was limited. To add insult to injury, Cameron Boozer suffered multiple orbital and facial fractures around his eye during the game (and played through it).

The two injured starters came off the bench. Ngongba finished with 6 points and 5 rebounds in 22 minutes. Foster also played 22 minutes, took one shot, and finished with 1 rebound, 2 assists, and 3 turnovers. People forget that, too.

They also forget that instead of junior Foster getting the ball on the last play, freshman Cayden Boozer did — and he made the kind of mistake a freshman can make.

Next play, next season. That next season is here, and Duke is a very different team.

Cameron Boozer is gone, drafted third overall by the Memphis Grizzlies and after his Summer League play, looking like a serious candidate for Rookie of the Year . Isaiah Evans is in Minnesota. Maliq Brown is a San Antonio Spur. Nik Khamenia transferred to UConn; Darren Harris went to Indiana. They will all be missed.

However, Scheyer has reloaded. Duke will not have Boozer's star power, but last season's injuries may have persuaded Scheyer to build a deeper roster. And we'll start with the returnees, all of whom are quite good.

Foster is back after a brutal spring and has grown into a real leader. We've been calling him captain already, even before the official announcement. He will be one.

Last year he averaged 8.3 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 0.3 steals, and 0.1 blocks in 24.7 minutes. He shot 44.7 percent from the field, 39.8 percent from three, and a pedestrian 58.2 percent from the line.

He is not an elite athlete. His lateral quickness is only average, and though he averaged just 1.1 turnovers, he is not a natural point guard. He is tough as nails, he takes care of the ball, and he loves being a Blue Devil. This should be his best year, assuming he stays healthy.

His performance against St. John's was sensational, but it was a one-off born of necessity.

Twenty days after surgery, he came off the bench with Duke down 10, having not played five-on-five since the operation. He was not in game shape, and the foot was nowhere close to 100 percent.

Still, it was something of a Willis Reed moment. Foster scored 11 straight points on four consecutive possessions, then got back on the scooter and left the floor with a win. As Bill Raftery might say: onions.

Ngongba also finished the season with a foot injury, but he played well before that point.

The 6-11 big man logged 21.9 minutes a night and averaged 10.1 points, 5.8 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 0.6 steals, and 1.1 blocks. He shot 60.6 percent from the field, 25.8 percent from three, and 66.4 percent from the line.

He is still an underrated passer. Last season he and Cameron Boozer had a knack for finding each other, and Brown got in on it too. All three moved the ball extremely well. Ngongba will have to find new targets, but do not underestimate him.

He is also an elite defender who takes away driving lanes and floaters. He was hitting his stride and looking like a sure first-round pick when the foot trouble started.

At times last year his emotions got the better of him, and that has to improve.

If he stays healthy, he can establish himself as one of the best big men in the country.

Cayden Boozer is back as well. He averaged 7.7 points, 2.3 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 0.8 steals, and 0.1 blocks. For a guard, the shooting was impressive: 50.0 percent from the field, 30.3 percent from three, and 81.3 percent from the line.

He grew as much as anyone on the team. His challenge now is to prove the glitch against UConn was a fluke. That play will follow him until he shows it does not define him.

When Foster went down in the regular-season finale against UNC, it could have wrecked Duke's March. Instead Boozer rose to the occasion and made the All-ACC Tournament team.

He is a wickedly smart player with a 7-0 wingspan, but there is work to do. The three-point shot was inconsistent and a bit flat. He is not wildly athletic, and he sometimes struggles to create his own shot. Intelligence is a skill, though, and Boozer has it in abundance.

People remember the turnover. They forget that he went 4-for-5 for 15 points, with 6 assists and 5 rebounds, in that same UConn game. That is pretty damn good.

Dame Sarr is back, too. His stat line — 6.4 points, 3.8 rebounds, 1.1 assists, 1.0 steal, and 0.4 blocks — does not begin to measure his impact. Sarr is a stunning on-ball defender with rare speed and endurance. Last season he would pick a guy up under the basket and hound him the length of the floor. On one occasion he stole the ball and took off the other way like he was spring-loaded. Honestly, we're not sure the last time we saw someone move that much faster than anyone else on a basketball court. It was breathtaking.

The offense was less clean. He shot 40.4 percent overall and 32.5 percent from deep.

Like Foster and Ngongba, he needs a lot of work at the line, where he hit just 53.2 percent. He also finished poorly in transition, missing far too many chippies. He looks stronger this year, which should help.

Finally, there is Sebastian Wilkins, who redshirted last season. We will find out soon enough where he is.

It probably won't happen, but you could start Duke's five returnees and be immensely competitive.

But there's more. Much more, actually, and we'll start to get into it in Part II.

articles.title: Predicting Bucks’ Three Most Likely Trade Candidates This Season
articles.summary: The Bucks have three veterans on their roster that they could flip for future assets.
articles.body:
This offseason, it was clear the Milwaukee Bucks shifted directions after trading star forward and former Finals MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo to the Miami Heat .

In return, they got an extra first-round pick, which they used on forward Nate Ament with the 13th overall pick in this year's draft, and they got players such as Tyler Herro , Jaime Jaquez Jr. , Kel'el Ware, and Kasparas Jakucionis .

The Bucks also held the rights to the 10th overall pick, which they used to draft guard Brayden Burries out of Arizona.

While the franchise has been working towards garnering assets for the future, its draft capital in the coming years is a question mark, and they don't have rights to its own first-round pick in 2027.

Because of this, they could be a team that sells various players during the season, and they could be active in trades. There are three veterans on this Bucks roster who could be up for grabs for contending teams.

One of those players is center Myles Turner . Turner is someone who just signed a big contract with the Bucks in 2025, but after the franchise's sudden change in direction by the franchise, he could be on the move sooner than most think.

While he's coming off a down year in 2025-2026, a change of scenery could help him get back into form. Turner likely expected to be competing for a championship with Giannis by his side upon his arrival, but now he's part of a rebuild.

Flipping Turner for draft capital or young players could help Milwaukee long-term, and a contending team may be willing to give what they want.

Another player who could be on the move before the end of the season is Caris LeVert . LeVert was traded to the Bucks from the Detroit Pistons this summer, but he could be elsewhere by the end of next season because he may not have a place on this roster.

One of Milwaukee's strengths is their backcourt. They have multiple young players at the position, and LeVert could be flipped for future assets.

Contending teams could use him for his scoring ability and veteran presence, which was his role last season with the Pistons. There is definitely a possibility that both sides could work on finding a trade partner by February.

The last trade candidate on the Bucks is guard A.J. Green. Green has been a reliable shooter for Milwaukee since 2022, and with a full rebuild happening, the front office could look to shop him around.

Contending teams could want Green, as he's only 26 years old and coming off another good shooting year. While it may be risky for Milwaukee to give him away, this is someone who could give them the most value of anyone else on the roster.

If the Bucks decide to trade Green, it could be because of an underwhelming season in which they see a lot of losses. All three of these players could be gone by March, and it will be interesting to see how the front office manages its roster as the season progresses.

articles.title: Could NY Giants Make Joey Porter Jr. Trade Soon? NYG Insider Adds Fuel to Speculation After Week 1 Win
articles.summary: A New York Giants trade for disgruntled Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. in the next few weeks is a […]
articles.body:
A New York Giants trade for disgruntled Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. in the next few weeks is a real possibility, according to a new report from a team insider.

On Sunday night, the Giants kicked off the John Harbaugh era with a strong performance against division rivals the Dallas Cowboys . The Cowboys entered the Week 1 matchup as a popular dark horse pick in the NFC; however, the new-look Giants pushed them around with a physical approach led by Jaxson Dart and their run game.

While the defense put forth a solid effort, a case can be made that the Giants dodged a bullet against a very talented Dallas defense that was rusty in their 2026 season debut. New York had no sacks, only three QB hits, and the Cowboys just missed on a few big plays in the passing game against a banged-up Big Blue cornerback corps.

Heading into Week 2, the Giants have four different corners on injured reserve. Fortunately for them, it is not their top corners, but their CB group wasn't a strength entering the season and could be a problem if their front seven doesn't get consistent pressure. That is why some have linked the team to the talented but unhappy Steelers cornerback.

Is a NY Giants trade for Joey Porter Jr. brewing?

But how likely is a Giants trade for Porter Jr. to improve their secondary? Well, according to the New York Post's Ryan Dunleavy, it is possible because Porter Jr. has fans inside the organization.

In a new conversation with Brandon Love, the Giants reporter claimed a trade in the next week or two "doesn't make sense" for the team, but it is "on the radar" for the front office. Dunleavy noted the Giants are happy with their CBs, but an injury could quickly change plans to pursue a trade.

"I had heard over the years that it was splitting hairs between Deonte Banks and Joey Porter Jr. in the 2023 draft. The Giants obviously went with Banks on a slight trade up, but there was a lot of interest in Porter. They had very similar grades in the building, talent-wise. The last two years, they looked foolish because Banks wasn't very good and Porter was… It's funny how these things go in a circle, and maybe in a couple of weeks they'll be teammates."

Porter Jr. is currently dealing with a back injury. However, many believe it is being used as a holdout excuse as he seeks a big-money contract extension, with this being the final season of his rookie contract. Although he hasn't earned year-end honors, the son of the Steelers is great is viewed as one of the best young corners in the AFC and would certainly be a huge addition for the Giants.

articles.title: Paul George Has No Problem Taking A Back Seat To Jayson Tatum
articles.summary: The Boston Celtics will have another star in the mix this season, but that does not mean the pecking order has to change. Paul George was asked whether he st...
articles.body:
The Boston Celtics will have another star in the mix this season, but that does not mean the pecking order has to change. Paul George was asked whether he still expects to be viewed as a superstar, and his answer pointed somewhere else.

George did not spend the moment selling himself. Instead, he made it clear that Jayson Tatum already holds the top spot in Boston, and he has no issue fitting around that role rather than trying to take it over.

Paul George Is Comfortable Letting Jayson Tatum Lead

George knows what it feels like to share a team with another elite wing. That experience appears to shape his approach in Boston, where the Celtics already have an established centerpiece in Tatum.

"We have a superstar, and that's JT. I'm not here to necessarily steal the shine or try to reinvent who I am …" George said when asked if he expects to still be a superstar.

That answer says plenty about what George expects from his role. He is not arriving in Boston to chase the biggest share of attention, and he does not seem interested in changing his game just to protect a superstar label.

For the Celtics, that could matter as much as any individual scoring total. A veteran who accepts the existing hierarchy gives the team more room to build an offense around its best player without creating an unnecessary fight for touches.

Paul George Has Shared The Spotlight Before

George also pointed to something he has already experienced during his career. He believes playing alongside another superstar wing can work when both players understand how to coexist.

"I've played alongside another superstar wing and we coexisted beautifully," George said.

That history gives his comments more weight. George is not describing a theory from the outside; he is drawing from his own experience and applying it to his next chapter in Boston.

Therefore, the Celtics do not need George to show that he is the star player. They need him to perform well while letting Tatum stay the main focus.

For George, that does not sound like a step backward. It sounds like a role he already knows can work.

articles.title: Here's how many people watched USA-France FIBA Women's World Cup final
articles.summary: TNT Sports has released the official viewership figure from Sunday's FIBA Women's World Cup final.
articles.body:
With Team USA being crowned the champion of the FIBA Women's World Cup for the fifth-straight tournament, the WNBA season will soon pick up.

Sunday's gold-medal matchup in Germany resulted in a 97-79 win for the U.S. over France, marking the Americans' record 12th time winning gold.

On Tuesday, TNT Sports released the total viewership figure from the final game of the tournament, setting a new record for the gold-medal matchup.

Here's a look at the viewership from the USA vs. France FIBA Women's World Cup final.

USA-France FIBA Women's World Cup final viewership

An average of 1.2 million people watched as Team USA took down France to win the tournament, TNT Sports said.

According to ESPN , that figure represented the third-highest FIBA Women's World Cup viewership on record, with the top two also coming from the 2026 tournament.

The final game peaked at 1.5 million viewers.

"It's a little bit of the planets aligning," executive vice president and chief content officer for TNT Sports Craig Barry told ESPN. "It's not just this great FIBA World Cup tournament, but women's sports coming into the spotlight the last three or four years."

The highest-rated game of the tournament was the United States' narrow win over Italy, which had an average of 1.3 million viewers, peaking at 1.7 million. The Americans ultimately won by three.

Before the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup, the highest-rated tournament game was the 2022 gold-medal matchup, which pulled in an average of 446,000 viewers on ESPN.

With the tournament now complete, the WNBA season will continue on Thursday, Sept. 17.

articles.title: How to watch Max vs 100
articles.summary: Max Verstappen is contesting a kart race against 100 competitors at Silverstone on Wednesday 16 September
articles.body:
Formula 1 world champion Max Verstappen is attempting a new challenge today (Wednesday 16 September) as he competes against 100 go-karters at Silverstone.

The event, run by Red Bull, is being dubbed as 'Max vs 100' and the Dutchman is racing against athletes, celebrities, content creators and everyday fans.

"In go-karts you learn all the basics: starts, defending, overtaking," said Verstappen. "Of course, I spent a long period of my life go-karting, so it's always nice to return

"It's about understanding the grip of the go-kart. I've done so many years in go-karting that you quite naturally get back into things."

Here is everything to know about the event.

Verstappen will start at the back of a 101-kart race and he has 30 laps - or a maximum of 55-75 minutes - to overtake his 100 rivals to win the contest. The grid order for the amateurs will be determined by qualifying - 2:20pm local time - where each karter gets one just flying lap with the session broken down into five segments of 20 drivers.

It is taking place on a purpose-built layout of the kart track at Silverstone and each time a driver is overtaken by the four-time F1 champion, they are eliminated from the event so it could easily end before the 30 laps are over.

The amateur drivers will have some assistance though, as at any point in the first half of the contest they can utilise what is called as a 'fast lap' which entails taking a shortcut on the track to try and put some further distance between them and Verstappen. But for the final 15 laps, Verstappen is the only one who can use a 'fast lap'.

That is the only advantage any driver will also have, because all the karts are identical and weigh 85kg with all included. Verstappen can also talk directly to his rivals via the radio.

Max vs 100 will be streamed live via ESPN on Disney+, which is commercial partner of Red Bull. Qualifying - 2:20pm-3:50pm local time - is not being broadcast but the race is and it starts at 6pm locally with the pre-event show starting at 5pm.

Comedian Mo Gilligan will present the coverage and there is no doubt going to be a large Mario Kart feel around it, as the broadcast will use game-inspired graphics and cinematic drone footage.

The entry list for Max vs 100 has been released and it includes a vast variety of personalities from British content creators like Zac Alsop and Jack McDermott - professionally known as Pieface - 2019 Love Island winner Amber Gill and ultramarathon runner Arda Saatci.

To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

articles.title: Eagles create cap space by converting Nolan Smith’s salary
articles.summary: Hmm. What do you think it means?
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles created some cap space in 2026 and 2027 by converting portions of Nolan Smith's salaries over the next two years into bonuses, according to Spotrac.

Are the Eagles about to sign Zach Ertz or make another big move?!

It's hardly uncommon for NFL teams — the Eagles included — to create cap space for flexibility purposes … and not necessarily because they immediately make a big move with the newly freed up funds. As a reminder, any cap space that the Eagles free up in the short-term will be rolled over into the future if it goes unused.

So, we'll see if Howie Roseman truly has something up his sleeve or not.

Prior to this move, the Eagles were listed at $12,371,633 in 2026 cap space from Over The Cap . For context, that ranked 13th-most in the league. They had $33,104,750 in 2027 cap space, which ranked 14th-most.

articles.title: Chesney praises UCLA offensive line for Wayne Knight's early success
articles.summary: "Wayne doesn't just score by himself," Chesney said. "He needs a whole lot of help and I think that those guys played a physical tough game up front."
articles.body:
The UCLA football team welcomed San Diego State to the Rose Bowl on Saturday evening for the Bruins ' home opener, which UCLA won 28-10 to remain unbeaten.

After the game, Bruins head coach Bob Chesney spoke to the media about the play of Wayne Knight . The senior running back rushed 13 times for 97 yards and three touchdowns.

"Obviously, he had three touchdowns (and) it was the first time he ever did it in his career. I didn't know that, and he did it twice in a row, so I think that's probably shown something even more than what people thought," Chesney said Saturday. "I think we all knew what he was pretty capable of and I thought, again – you watch Wayne, but let's just talk a little bit about the offensive line in there as well from (the offensive line) pulling around on that one run, it was violent at the point of attack like he was and then the receiver's blocking on the outside. "Wayne doesn't just score by himself. He needs a whole lot of help and I think that those guys played a physical tough game up front which allowed him to have the success that he had and I think he'd be the first to say that."

"Obviously, he had three touchdowns (and) it was the first time he ever did it in his career. I didn't know that, and he did it twice in a row, so I think that's probably shown something even more than what people thought," Chesney said Saturday. "I think we all knew what he was pretty capable of and I thought, again – you watch Wayne, but let's just talk a little bit about the offensive line in there as well from (the offensive line) pulling around on that one run, it was violent at the point of attack like he was and then the receiver's blocking on the outside.

"Wayne doesn't just score by himself. He needs a whole lot of help and I think that those guys played a physical tough game up front which allowed him to have the success that he had and I think he'd be the first to say that."

articles.title: Simon Edvinsson’s Agent Reveals Major Development After Red Wings GM Announcement
articles.summary: Simon Edvinsson’s agent says contract talks are underway with Shawn Horcoff following the Red Wings’ interim GM announcement.
articles.body:
Shawn Horcoff's appointment has brought movement on one of the Detroit Red Wings' most pressing contract decisions.

Simon Edvinsson's agent, J.P. Barry, told Expressen's Gunnar Nordstrom that discussions are underway with Detroit's interim general manager. The update follows Tuesday's announcement that Horcoff would take over the GM position while the organization continues searching for its permanent hockey operations leader.

"We were talking to him today. He now has authority to negotiate on behalf of the team ," Barry said, according to The Malik Report's English translation of the Expressen report.

That gives Detroit something tangible following the leadership announcement: an active negotiation involving a key defenseman.

It also answers an immediate question about Horcoff's assignment. His interim status allows the organization to conduct important contract business while Chris Ilitch evaluates candidates for the permanent position.

Simon Edvinsson Contract Talks Move Forward

According to the translated report, the sides are discussing a multiyear agreement. Barry expressed hope that a deal could be reached before the regular season begins.

The report does not announce an agreement or establish that the sides are close on salary and term.

That distinction matters for Detroit. Opening discussions is a necessary step, but the length and cost of an Edvinsson contract will determine how the commitment fits into the team's longer-term roster planning.

For Horcoff, the negotiation offers an early opportunity to produce a concrete result. As Reuters reported when Detroit announced the appointment , his responsibilities include roster decisions and salary-cap management.

The title may be temporary. The consequences of a multiyear agreement would extend well beyond the search for a permanent executive.

Detroit's Leadership Search Continues Alongside Negotiations

Ilitch has left open the possibility that the permanent leadership hire could wait until after the season . That makes Horcoff's ability to handle current business essential.

Detroit cannot treat every unresolved roster matter as something for the next executive to inherit. Edvinsson's negotiations illustrate why the organization needs someone empowered to make decisions now.

Barry's update supplies evidence that those conversations are happening. The next significant development will be whether the sides can turn that contact into a signed contract.

articles.title: Nets star predicts 50-win season in Brooklyn
articles.summary: Michael Porter Jr. has wild expectations for this year's Nets squad.
articles.body:
Michael Porter Jr . has a habit of saying things that make people raise their eyebrows. The latest episode of his podcast, " Curious Mike ," features an interview with an adult film actress, but that's not what has people doing a double-take this week. During a recent conversation with streamer N3on, he laid out the case for the Brooklyn Nets to win 50 games this season.

That would be two-and-a-half times the number of games they won last season. It would be more than they won in the previous two seasons combined. It is a truly outrageous thought.

Porter explained the key is his chemistry with Julius Randle .

Michael Porter Jr. says the Brooklyn Nets will win 50+ games this upcoming season 👀 (Via @N3onOnYT ) pic.twitter.com/DVeFONtpoM — Fullcourtpass (@Fullcourtpass) September 16, 2026

Michael Porter Jr. says the Brooklyn Nets will win 50+ games this upcoming season 👀 (Via @N3onOnYT ) pic.twitter.com/DVeFONtpoM

Fullcourtpass (@Fullcourtpass) September 16, 2026

"I think if we get that chemistry right, all of our young guys from last year got so much better bro. We're like … I don't know what the expectations are for our team, but we're gonna definitely surpass that."

Porter wasn't the one to come up with that number, but when N3on asked if the Nets would pass the 50-win mark, he said yes. This would be wild. Brooklyn hasn't won 50 games in more than two decades. They went 52-30 in the 2001-02 season when Jason Kidd was the point guard and they made the NBA Finals. That's how good a 50-win team is. A team that wins 50 or more games is in the title conversation.

Only seven teams in the whole league won 50 or more games last season. The Knicks , who won the title, went 53-29.

Sniffing .500 would be an incredible achievement for the Nets this year. It would have them in the conversation to be a play-in team. They haven't made the playoffs or finished over .500 since Kevin Durant and Kyrie Irving left.

It would also be one of the biggest single-season turnarounds in NBA history. Just getting to 50 would be the seventh-largest single-season turnaround in NBA history. It would put them right behind the Celtics during Larry Bird's rookie season in 1979 and ahead of the Milwaukee Bucks when they drafted Lew Alcindor, who later changed his name to Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, in 1969.

Don't ever say Michael Porter Jr. isn't an optimist.

articles.title: WWE news: Simone Johnson recalls catching flak after The Rock took Cody Rhodes' WrestleMania spot
articles.summary: A few years ago, Cody Rhodes almost missed out on finishing his story at WWE WrestleMania 40. Despite winning his second Royal Rumble in a row, Rhodes was a...
articles.body:
A few years ago, Cody Rhodes almost missed out on finishing his story at WWE WrestleMania 40 . Despite winning his second Royal Rumble in a row, Rhodes was almost kicked out of his WrestleMania 40 spot against Roman Reigns when "The Rock" returned and seemingly hijacked it.

While Dwayne Johnson's WWE return was appreciated, fans were strongly against him taking Rhodes' hard-earned spot . Fans across the globe hijacked WWE's social media and let their frustrations known. However, the flak also spread to Johnson's daughter, Simone Johnson, aka Ava Raine, who also received major hate on her socials.

Recently appearing on Cody Rhodes' Cody on What Do You Want To Talk About? podcast, Johnson recalled the flak she received after her father potentially took "The American Nightmare's" chance of finishing his story . (via Fightful)

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Dad [The Rock] came back; he shook your hand; he took your spot. That was Friday. That Sunday was a NXT pay-per-view, Vengeance Day. It was the first time there was WWE programming since that Friday. I will never forget this. I was sitting in makeup. I finished my makeup, and our head writer, Johnny Russo, came up to me and was like, 'Can I talk to you for a minute?' 'Sure.' I don't think I had filmed the promo that I was doing that day; we were about to film it.

"He was like, 'Just so you know, when we play your promo, please don't be surprised if they boo you.' 'Okay.' I can understand that. That did happen. All of the hate online happened. That day, it changed the way I looked at fans overall and changed the way that I looked at the wrestling business. For a while, I thought about it in a very negative way. It was quite negative at the time," she recalled.

However, despite receiving the hate, Johnson revealed that she was grateful that it happened, because it helped her become more confident. "All these external factors are happening, and everyone can have an opinion because of who I am or what my dad has done. It made me be a little selfish in my journey and what I was doing, but it was necessary," she added.

However, things later worked out, and Rhodes was able to finish his story against Reigns at WrestleMania 40, while "The Rock" main-evented WrestleMania 40 Night One.

Raine was a part of the WWE NXT roster from 2020 to 2026, where she worked as both an in-ring talent and the brand's general manager in her final reign. In Jan. 2026, Raine decided to not renew her WWE contract and willingly let it expire.

articles.title: Tiger Woods Spotted On The Driving Range, Fueling Rumors
articles.summary: Tiger Woods is hitting golf balls again, and the 15-time major champion offered a striking assessment of what he can do with a club in his hands. “I can hit...
articles.body:
Tiger Woods is hitting golf balls again, and the 15-time major champion offered a striking assessment of what he can do with a club in his hands.

"I can hit pretty much anything," Woods said after returning to the range for the first time since a car crash six months ago.

Woods, 50, was filmed hitting balls at Liberty National in New Jersey ahead of the Nexus Cup, a charity event he is hosting to raise money for his TGR Foundation. The session was shared on Instagram, giving golf fans a rare look at Woods swinging a club after another lengthy period away from competitive play.

He also held a clinic at the event. When the master of ceremonies asked about the state of his game, Woods kept it short: "I can hit pretty much anything."

Another Tiger Woods Comeback Remains Uncertain

Whether that means another competitive comeback is coming remains unclear.

Woods has not played competitively since 2024. He ruptured an Achilles tendon in March 2025 and underwent back surgery last October, adding to an extensive list of injuries that have repeatedly interrupted his career.

His latest return to the range comes six months after a road accident in Florida in which Woods rolled his Land Rover and had to crawl from the vehicle through the passenger door. He refused a urine test following the crash.

Earlier this month, Woods accepted a five-year suspension of his driving license and a $1,000 fine under a plea agreement with prosecutors in Martin County, Florida, after he did not contest a reckless driving charge.

Following the March accident, Woods announced that he was stepping away temporarily.

"I'm stepping away for a period of time to seek treatment and focus on my health," he said.

Woods Has Faced Driving Incidents Before

The crash was the latest driving-related incident involving Woods. In 2017, he received a year of probation after pleading guilty to reckless driving following an incident in which police found him slumped behind the wheel of his vehicle near his home.

Woods also survived a serious single-car crash in California in 2021 that caused extensive injuries to his right leg. His competitive schedule was severely limited afterward, with Woods making only sporadic tournament appearances as he dealt with the physical consequences.

His difficulties away from competition stretch back further. In 2009, Woods crashed into a fire hydrant, a tree and hedges outside his Florida home amid revelations about extramarital affairs. His marriage subsequently ended, and he lost major sponsorship agreements.

Now, after injuries, surgeries and another road accident, the sight of Woods back on a driving range inevitably raises the question that has followed almost every stage of his later career: Will he try to return?

For the moment, Woods has not announced a competitive comeback or provided a timetable for one. A range session is a long way from walking multiple rounds of tournament golf under competitive conditions. But six months after crawling out of a wrecked vehicle, Woods was back at Liberty National with a club in his hands.

articles.title: 3 areas where the Ravens can still improve following a dominant opener
articles.summary: The Ravens opened the season with an impressive victory, but as is the case with every team, there's still plenty of room for growth.
articles.body:
Stop the presses if you have heard this before, but the Baltimore Ravens couldn't have drawn up a much better opening act on the road vs. the Indianapolis Colts . Baltimore piled up more than 500 yards of offense, forced two turnovers, rushed for over 200 yards, and left Lucas Oil Stadium with a convincing 41-23 victory .

They were breaking in a new coaching staff and two first-time starters on the offensive line, Vega Ioane and Jovaughn Gwyn . There was plenty to like. The Ravens looked explosive, physical, and capable of winning in multiple ways. Still, nobody inside the building is treating Week 1 as a finished product. Kyle Hamilton graded the defense as average, while Derrick Henry 's postgame message focused on avoiding complacency after a strong start. With a home matchup against the New Orleans Saints looming, here are three areas where Baltimore can still improve.

Clean up the penalties and self-inflicted mistakes

Again, stop us if you have heard this before. The final score suggests Baltimore cruised, but the Ravens repeatedly got in their own way. Baltimore was flagged 10 times for 86 yards , and several of those penalties erased game-changing plays. Ja'Kobi Lane appeared to have his first NFL touchdown before a holding penalty wiped it off the board. Rashod Bateman converted a key third down, but it also disappeared because of a flag. Chris Moore delivered a 49-yard return that would have flipped field position, only to see it called back.

The Ravens were the better team throughout the afternoon, but penalties kept Indianapolis within striking distance longer than necessary. Cut those mistakes in half, and the margin of victory could have been even larger. It seems the Saints can't win in Week 2 unless the Ravens help them

Baltimore's passing attack looked dynamic early, especially with Zay Flowers stretching the field. Flowers accounted for 150 receiving yards in the first half before exiting with a hamstring issue, and the offense understandably lost some of its explosiveness afterward.

The situation became more complicated when Ja'Kobi Lane suffered a fractured wrist. After the news broke, CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz reported that Lane is expected to undergo surgery, with the current hope that he can return in roughly a month.

Chris Moore's 53-yard catch helped close out the win, and the veteran could see a larger role moving forward . Meanwhile, Devontez Walker missed Week 1 with a groin injury, and Elijah Sarratt was inactive despite being healthy. Baltimore may need both players involved sooner rather than later.

The offensive line dominated as a run-blocking unit, helping Henry score three rushing touchdowns and powering Baltimore's 202-yard rushing performance. Pass protection told a slightly different story. According to Pro Football Focus, the Ravens allowed 10 pressures on 33 pass plays. Lamar Jackson was sacked twice and faced several snaps in which pressure arrived much faster than Baltimore would prefer.

The contrast showed up in the Pro Football Focus grades. Notice the numbers:

PFF run-blocking grades for the Ravens offensive line

PFF pass-blocking grades for the Ravens offensive line

Raise your hand if anything jumps out at you. Don't adjust your screens or restate your devices. These aren't misprints.

Gwyn earned an outstanding run-blocking mark but struggled in pass protection, while veteran guard John Simpson also posted a significantly lower pass-blocking grade than his run-blocking score.

Considering two starters were making their first NFL starts, some inconsistency was expected. The encouraging part is that pass protection issues are often easier to correct than physical shortcomings. If Baltimore cleans up the penalties, gets healthier at receiver, and improves protection, an already impressive Week 1 performance could look even better in the weeks ahead.

images.caption: 3 areas where the Ravens can still improve following a dominant opener

articles.title: 3 obvious areas where Eagles can improve entering road clash vs. Titans
articles.summary: Despite escaping Week 1 with a victory, the areas of opportunity remain obvious as the Eagles prepare for a rod trip vs. the Titans.
articles.body:
The difference between panic and perspective often comes down to one play. Had the Washington Commanders converted their late two-point attempt, the conversation surrounding the Philadelphia Eagles would be dramatically different this week.

Instead, Philadelphia escaped Week 1 with a 24-22 victory , improved to 1-0, and extended the Jalen Hurts-Nick Sirianni era's perfect record in season openers . That doesn't mean everything went according to plan.

The Eagles generated enough explosive plays to win. Hurts delivered another clutch performance when the game hung in the balance. They made the defensive stop they absolutely needed. They also struggled to sustain drives, received uneven play from the offensive line, and left several opportunities on the field. The good news is none of the issues appear fatal. The bad news is they'll need to improve quickly with a road trip to face the Tennessee Titans looming. Before the Eagles take the field in Week 2, here are three obvious areas that need improvement.

The offensive line leaves much to be desired.

Pro Football Focus released its Week 1 grades . They weren't particularly flattering to Philadelphia's offensive front.

PFF grades should never be treated as gospel, but they often help identify trends. In this case, the numbers largely reinforce what many saw Sunday.

Philadelphia's offensive line struggled to create consistent movement in the running game, and communication breakdowns occasionally left defenders unaccounted for. Sean Mannion referenced those issues multiple times during his media availability, repeatedly mentioning the need to stay on schedule and clean up communication up front.

The challenge only grows with Landon Dickerson now on injured reserve. Whether it's Drew Kendall or Willie Lampkin, the Eagles need more consistency from a unit that has long been the foundation of their offense.

There were plenty of highlights. Hurts threw three touchdown passes. Dallas Goedert hauled in two scores. Dontayvion Wicks and DeVonta Smith provided two of the game's biggest explosive plays. Hurts also delivered arguably the play of the game when he scrambled 22 yards on third-and-18 late in the fourth quarter.

The problem is those moments often felt isolated rather than connected. Philadelphia finished with five three-and-outs and spent too much of the afternoon fighting long-yardage situations. The Eagles repeatedly relied on difficult third-down conversions rather than staying ahead of the chains.

That concern isn't new. One of the major criticisms of last year's offense was its inability to sustain drives and consistently control games for four quarters. Through one week, some of those same concerns remain. The encouraging part is, if the offensive line settles in and the Eagles avoid negative plays, the rhythm should follow.

The pass rush must finish when opportunities arise

The Eagles generated pressure. The problem is they didn't generate enough sacks. According to Washington Post reporter Tashan Reed, the Commanders allowed pressure on roughly half of Jayden Daniels' dropbacks. Yet Philadelphia finished with only one sack.

Vic Fangio wasn't particularly pleased with what he saw. The defensive coordinator said the pass rush "wasn't good enough" and pointed to a lack of one-on-one victories across the board. Mobile quarterbacks can create challenges, and Daniels certainly did that throughout the afternoon, but the Eagles need better finishing ability from their front.

The Titans present another opportunity this week. Cam Ward remains dangerous because of his mobility, but he also held the football at times during Tennessee's opener against the New York Jets. If the Eagles generate the same level of pressure they produced against Washington, they'll need to do a better job turning those opportunities into drive-killing sacks.

The encouraging part is that none of these issues feel impossible to fix. The Eagles aren't searching for answers after a blowout loss. They're trying to clean up mistakes following a victory. That's a big difference.

Philadelphia already proved it can win while playing less than its best football. Now comes the harder part. The Titans won't care that the Eagles escaped Week 1. Tennessee will look to exploit the same weaknesses Washington exposed. If Philadelphia improves its offensive line play, sustains drives more consistently, and finishes plays defensively, there's every reason to believe a cleaner performance awaits in Week 2.

Ticket sales for Bologna vs. Inter , to be played at the Dall'Ara on Saturday 17 October at 18:00 CEST, opened today. Until 22:00 CEST on 16 September, tickets are available exclusively for 26/27 season-ticket holders, who can purchase up to four tickets (Plus season ticket) or two tickets (Basic season ticket) in a single transaction. From 10:00 CEST on 17 September, tickets will be available to everyone, both online and at points of sale. Full ticket information

articles.title: Vote for the Journal Sentinel play of the week for the week of Sept. 7
articles.summary: Vote from five nominations for the best high school play in the weekly Milwaukee Journal Sentinel poll for the week of Sept. 7, 2026.
articles.body:
What was the best play in the Milwaukee area this past week? You tell us.

This past week featured five excellent plays from Week 4 action of high school football around the area and you can decide by voting for the best one from now until noon on Saturday, Sept. 19, as many times as you'd like.

We now have a submission tool on our Preps Plus portion of the Journal Sentinel website. The location to upload your clips is under the top banner that's labeled " Upload Your Video ". It's a four-step process that will allow you to upload clips from the week across all fall sports. The clips must be trimmed and uploaded to be 30 seconds or shorter in the proper formatting to be eligible for selection. Please submit your clips by the end of the day on Mondays to make sure your clip is potentially included to be a nominee.

If you have any questions about submitting a play of the week nominee, contact Michael Whitlow via email at mwhitlow@gannett.com.

Menomonee Falls football vs. Whitefish Bay on Sept. 10

Ben Prescher, jr., Arrowhead: Prescher caught two passes for 25 yards with a 12-yard touchdown grab being the best of the bunch in Arrowhead's 45-21 victory over Brookfield East last week. The junior has caught seven balls this season, but three of them have gone for scores through the first four weeks.

Aiden Goines, jr., Menomonee Falls: Despite a 22-18 defeat to Whitefish Bay last week, Aiden Goines continued to do what he has done all season for the Phoenix and that's make big plays. Goines caught four passes for 107 yards and this 93-yard catch-and-run score against the Blue Dukes.

Keegan Degeorge, sr., Waukesha South: The star wideout was on his way to a massive night against Greenfield last week, but an ankle injury hindered that opportunity. Despite an ineligible man downfield penalty taking this touchdown off the board, Degeorge made an insane catch through traffic. He would finish with four catches for 76 yards and a 19-yard touchdown.

Mekhi Malcom, sr., Wauwatosa East: Despite the Red Raiders suffering their first defeat last week to Pewaukee, the two-way senior found a way to make an impact. He caught four passes offensively and also made a great play on this interception in Tosa East's 27-8 loss to the Pirates.

Lateef Love Jr., sr., Whitefish Bay: Was he down? The whistle didn't blow? What in the world? Regardless, it was a 10-yard touchdown run for Lateef Love Jr. on this weird play in the Blue Dukes' 22-18 victory over Menomonee Falls last week. Love Jr. would finish with 21 carries for 159 yards and this wild touchdown.

articles.title: Kingsley Enagbare was exactly what the Jets needed him to be in Week 1
articles.summary: Veteran defensive end Kingsley Enagbare was exactly what the New York Jets needed him to be in Week 1.
articles.body:
The New York Jets got to debut their new-look defense in Week 1.

It was a dominant performance, having defeated the Tennessee Titans 23-10 while holding their offense under 200 yards. Veteran defensive end Kingsley Enagbare was among the new Jets defenders who made a good first impression.

The Jets signed Enagbare to a one-year contract worth $9 million in free agency this past offseason. The former South Carolina standout was acquired to bring early-down toughness to the Jets' revamped defensive line . That's exactly what Enagbare did versus the Titans in Week 1.

Pro Football Focus credited Enagbare with registering five pressures and one sack. Titans offensive tackles Dan Moore Jr. and JC Latham had no answer for his balanced skill set as a pass rusher and run stopper. Enagbare's PFF pass-rushing score was a stellar 70.5.

Enagbare played the second-most snaps (33) among all Jets defensive ends in Week 1. Rookie David Bailey played a position-high 35 snaps . The Jets basically used Enagbare as an early-down base end, with Will McDonald IV rotating in to play 25 snaps.

The Jets had a quality plan for Enagbare in Week 1. It was a very positive debut for the veteran defender. Hopefully Enagbare continues providing the Jets with high-level play.

articles.title: ‘I felt somewhat disrespected’ – Beşiktaş’ Amir Murillo on relationship with Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi at Marseille
articles.summary: Roberto De Zerbi will not have left an indelible mark on his time at Olympique de Marseille. Or at least, perhaps not in the way he would have hoped. This go...
articles.body:
Roberto De Zerbi will not have left an indelible mark on his time at Olympique de Marseille . Or at least, perhaps not in the way he would have hoped. This goes for his supporters, as well as his players.

Just a few hours before reuniting with his former team-mates for the opening match of the Europa League group stage, Beşiktaş JK defender Amir Murillo (30), who joined from OM last February, used his appearance at a press conference to settle scores with the Italian manager.

"Everyone saw that I'd had a problem with the manager," recalled the Panamanian left-back. "It had nothing to do with the club, nor with the team. I think it was simply something personal on the manager's part and that, in a way, I felt it was a lack of respect. They practically forced me to leave the club, and that's how I ended up at Beşiktaş."

Having left Marseille barely a week later, De Zerbi went on to take up the managerial post at Tottenham Hotspur, a role he still holds today, with a record of four wins, four draws and five defeats since his arrival.

articles.title: Pressley on injury troubles, Graham call-up & wounded Motherwell
articles.summary: Steven Pressley has been speaking to the media before Dundee host Motherwell in the Premiership on Saturday (15:00 BST).  With a handful of players sidelined...
articles.body:
Steven Pressley has been speaking to the media before Dundee host Motherwell in the Premiership on Saturday (15:00 BST).

With a handful of players sidelined, Pressley admits: "It is probably one of the most challenging periods, in terms of injuries, in my time as a head coach."

But he joked it makes the team selection a bit easier because there are fewer players to let down.

On facing a Motherwell side thrashed 4-0 at home by Aberdeen on Tuesday, Pressley says "often a wounded animal is a very dangerous proposition".

He adds Motherwell have the second-highest possession in the league and "know what they are doing".

Pressley says if Dundee can win and go into the international break with 10 points from their opening seven games it would represent a "really positive start for us".

"We couldn't be prouder" after former Dundee defender Luke Graham was called into the senior Scotland squad, with Pressley saying he deserves the opportunity and can a Scotland regular "for many years to come".

The Dens boss praised Graham for his football journey - "he was happy to do the hard yards" and is getting his rewards - and says Dundee having stories like that to tell may help sell the club to potential future signings.

Team news: Joe Westley and Ryan Finnigan are doubts. Simon Murray, Fin Robertson, Ash Hay, Charlie Reilly and Joe Wright are all out injured, while Zan Besir is suspended.
authors: Tyrone Smith - BBC Sport Scotland Senior Reporter

articles.title: Bogle voted Hisense Player of the Match after Newcastle victory
articles.summary: Jayden Bogle has been voted the Hisense Player of the Match following Leeds United’s 4-1 victory over Newcastle United at Elland Road on Monday night.The 26-...
articles.body:
Jayden Bogle has been voted the Hisense Player of the Match following Leeds United 's 4-1 victory over Newcastle United at Elland Road on Monday night.

The 26-year-old played 83 minutes before being replaced by Daniel James , producing an energetic display as the Whites secured a fourth consecutive unbeaten league game.

Bogle was credited with Leeds' second goal of the evening, although the strike took a slight touch off him.

James Justin 's dangerous delivery was met by Dominic Calvert-Lewin , whose header looked destined for the corner before brushing Bogle on its way into the net.

He finished the match with 41 touches and completed 15 passes , including four line-breaking passes and one key pass . He also registered three shots .

The defender covered 10km during his time on the pitch, completing 16 sprints and reaching a top speed of 32km/h .

He also made eight carries for a total distance of 94.1 metres , while winning 100 per cent of his tackles and four duels , as well as making one clearance and one recovery .

His performance also proved valuable for Fantasy Premier League managers, with the defender generating 15 points .

The voting was close, with Bogle receiving 27% of the vote. Tarik Muharemović was second with 25%, followed by Calvert-Lewin (19%) and Ao Tanaka (18%).
